title: Bengaluru City railway station
insights: The KSR Bengaluru railway station is a major transportation hub in Bengaluru, serving as the main railway station in the city. The station has a long history, dating back to the 19th century, and has undergone significant developments over the years, including the conversion of metre-gauge lines to broad gauge and the introduction of modern facilities such as digital lockers and child-friendly spaces. The station is well-connected to other parts of the city, with a metro station and a bus station nearby. The Bengaluru Suburban Railway, currently under construction, will further enhance the station's connectivity, with two corridors serving the station. The ridership at the metro station has seen a significant increase after the opening of the foot overbridge, indicating the importance of convenient connections between different modes of transport.

title: Electronic City
insights: Electronic City in Bengaluru, India, has developed significantly with a large number of IT/ITES companies, including major players like Infosys, Wipro, and TCS. The area has a well-established infrastructure in terms of connectivity, with BMTC bus services being the most popular mode of transport. The elevated expressway from Silk Board junction to Electronic City has reduced travel time, and the NICE road connects Electronic City to other key areas in the west of Bengaluru city. The Metro rail and suburban rail services also provide convenient transportation options. However, the area still faces challenges such as traffic congestion and safety concerns on the elevated expressway.

title: [PDF] Deep Dive City Bangalore, India
insights: The city of Bangalore has a population of 13.6 million with a growth rate of 3.14%, and a density of over 4 inhabitants per square kilometer, making it one of the fastest-growing cities in India. The city's transport system is dominated by public transport, accounting for 42% of all trips, followed by 2-wheelers at 29%. The city aims to improve its air quality by promoting e-mobility, with a target of operating 13,500 e-buses by 2030, which is expected to reduce emissions by 0.35 MtCO2 annually and improve the city's PM2.5 concentration by 1.75 μg/m3.

title: [PDF] Bengaluru - Asian Transport Observatory
insights: Bengaluru has a high block density of 83 blocks per sqkm and a population density of 25,000 people/sqkm, indicating a compact structure of population distribution. However, the city has limited green areas, with only 4% of the population living in high green areas, and limited car-free spaces, with only 23% of the population living near them. The city also has a low allocation of land for transportation and communications, at 7.3%, which is below the general norm of 15-20%. The city's built-up area per capita is also relatively low, at 25 sqm/capita.
